scope: Actual final README, starter, oracle, completed shortcut, independent reference, public/private tests, validator, metadata, runtime, AUTHOR and final reports were read. Every provenance payload hash was verified. No scientific or model evaluation was rerun and no task source was edited.
physics_findings: The prepared compact longitudinal distribution is normalized and single-peaked. The electron charge, self-consistent total field, periodic induced potential and external field amplitude fix the kinetic and Poisson signs.

The stated remote-past exp(eta*t) forcing, with amplitude taken to zero before eta, selects the causal boundary value. This avoids relying on decay of undamped compact-support collective modes after an arbitrary sudden switch.

The starter implements the full real principal-value response and Poisson self-consistency correctly. It is a coherent time-symmetric resonant closure, but its physical preparation differs from the actual adiabatically driven experiment. This is not a source that first obtains the correct complex causal dielectric and merely discards a plotted quadrature.

With exp[i(k*x-omega*t)], the kinetic denominator is u-z-i0 and the causal susceptibility is H_PV+i*pi*Fprime. The oracle sign, static H=-5, density/(k*width)^2 factor and real inverse-dielectric readout are consistent.

The detector integral 2/(L*amplitude) against cos(k*x) at t=0 returns precisely the real transfer. It contains no averaging or normalization ambiguity. Only in-phase response is scored; it does not by itself distinguish complex-conjugate causal and anti-causal transfer functions.

Static transfer is strictly decreasing in density over the full public interval and establishes global identification. Outside-support nonzero-frequency controls agree exactly between both response laws. Finite drive frequencies and all geometry controls are used by the starter.

The frequency windows avoid logarithmic endpoints and both source and physical dielectric poles. The reported denominator lower bounds .5708666 and .7300184 follow from the stated monotonic susceptibility bounds, not from a hidden restriction applied after evaluation.
reference_findings: The reference independently solves the causal Duhamel memory relation in frequency space at finite positive switch rates. Its time kernel is the characteristic function of the supplied velocity distribution; no PV logarithm or resonant jump is imported from the oracle.

Composite Gauss-Legendre integration, an explicit exponential tail bound, 16-to-24 order comparison and halved switch-rate extrapolation establish adequate numerical separation. The final results are comfortably below the ordinary .04 prediction gate.

The initial weighted infinite-interval quadrature and warning-bearing reports are preserved. The final change is a pre-evaluation integration-method correction only, with calibration bytes, source physics, oracle and grading unchanged. It is not a replaced model trial.

public_input_findings.required_apparatus_only: Velocity preparation, external-field switching, self-consistency, phase and ordered limits are necessary to specify the experiment. No Landau, contour, principal-value or missing-response diagnosis appears in the public README.

calibration.identifiability: Static transfer 1/(1+5*density/(k*width)^2) is strictly decreasing over the entire interval.

classification_guard: No empirical model difficulty is claimed before evaluation. A future failed trajectory must be read: retaining the time-symmetric preparation is the intended physical failure; an attempted causal solution with normalization, logarithm, sign or implementation defects is not automatically a clean physical failure.
